items.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
items.snippet: Modern LLM agents are often improved by modifying prompts, tools, or workflows manually, while the executable scaffold surrounding the model---the harness---is typically treated as a fixed artifact after deployment. items.summary: Framework for continuous task-specific evolution of LLM agent harnesses. Addresses automated improvement of deployment scaffolding beyond model weights.

items.title: The Embedder's Dilemma: LLMs Are Better, but at What Cost?
items.snippet: Should you replace your text-embedding pipeline with a large language model? We answer this with a controlled, cost-aware comparison of ten LLMs across six families and 26 embedding models (118M to 14B parameters) on 37 tasks spanning classification, semantic textual similarity (STS), clustering, pair classification, and retrieval. items.summary: Controlled cost-aware comparison of 26 embedding models (118M-14B) across 37 tasks. Practical benchmark for embedding pipeline decisions.

items.summary: FlowEvo: system for co-evolving LLM agent workflows and executable skills at runtime. Enables persistent skill library growth from deployment experience.

items.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
items.snippet: Large language model agents have made substantial progress in code generation, yet most existing systems assume a predefined repository architecture. This assumption does not hold in zero-to-all code generation, where an agent must construct an entire software project directly from natural-language requirements while maintaining a modular repository architecture throughout development. We present
items.summary: Repo0: agent-based code generation system for zero-to-all project construction from natural language. Relevant for understanding code generation and agentic workflows.

items.snippet: Take three frontier mixture-of-experts models (Alibaba, OpenAI, NVIDIA; 3.6-4.0B active parameters each) and fine-tune them to reason in a low-resource language. items.summary: Analysis of mixture-of-experts models fine-tuned for low-resource language reasoning, examining SFT vs RL tradeoffs. Insights on model capability transfer.

items.snippet: Using reinforcement learning to post-train joint video-audio generation models requires a reward signal. items.summary: VA-Judger: reward model for joint video-audio generation using human preference feedback. Relevant for multimodal model training and RLHF approaches.

items.title: τ_0-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
items.snippet: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to both execute individual skills reliably and sequence them coherently over extended tasks. items.summary: τ_0-VLA: hierarchical vision-language-action robot model with test-time computation allocation. Relevant for multimodal foundation models and resource-efficient inference.

items.title: QuoteBench: How Matched Scores Can Hide Command-Path Failures
items.snippet: LLM coding agents issue Bash commands through interfaces that may serialize, wrap, and reparse model output. items.summary: QuoteBench: evaluation framework for Bash command generation in LLM agents distinguishing generation errors from post-generation failures. Addresses coding agent reliability.
